Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the recent demo — Mosaic is moving this through procurement and we need to lock a couple of items in the MSA / Order Form before legal will greenlight signature: SOC 2 access, pen-test notice/coordination language, and a clear cadence for evidence delivery (SOC 2 report, pen-test attestation, config screenshots).

High-level asks from our side: 
- Mutual audit rights for SOC 2 and the ability to request pen-test evidence from your vendor (redacted)
- Pen test window: we expect 30 days notice and a stated non-production target to avoid impacting our customers
- Evidence cadence: supporting artifacts quarterly (or on request with 5 business days turnaround)

I attached a short spreadsheet with our standard security exhibit bullets. Can you confirm Redwood’s position and provide a proposed redline for the MSA + Order Form? Also suggest a proposed timeline for legal review so procurement can set expectations.

Appreciate it — we’re targeting signature by end of month if we can close these quickly.

Hi all — security perspective below. I kept this high level so Neha can sink it into contract language.

1) SOC 2 access & reports
- Redwood will provide a current SOC 2 Type II report on request via a secure portal (redacted for customer-specific data). Typical turnaround for ad-hoc requests is 10 business days to provide the latest report or confirm availability.
- For continuous evidence (e.g., logs/config snapshots), we can provide quarterly exports limited to scope agreed in the exhibit (security controls, access logs), subject to export/PII minimization.

2) Pen tests
- Redwood will accept customer-requested penetration tests provided: (a) tests are performed only against a non-production environment, (b) they are limited in scope to avoid production impact, and (c) the customer provides at least 15 business days notice to Redwood with test plan and vendor details.
- Redwood will provide vendor attestation of remediation for high/critical findings within 30 days of discovery; lower severity items will follow a standard remediation SLT.

3) Audit rights / mutuality
- We propose mutual rights only for SOC 2 and specific vendor-supplied pen-test attestations; broad operational audits (ad-hoc on-site efforts) are not feasible.

4) Evidence cadence
- Preferred: Quarterly bundled evidence packet (SOC 2 report + selected configuration snapshots) + ad-hoc requests for SOC 2 within 10 business days. For pen-test attestations, 30 days from vendor report to provide remediation confirmation.

I attached our initial tracked redline for the MSA & exhibit (file: 2026-07-07_Redwood_MSA_redlines.docx). Neha — happy to sync on tighter language. Samantha — if Mosaic requires a stricter 30-day notice for pen tests, flag it and we can escalate to product/infra to evaluate impact.

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 11:05:28 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA: SOC 2 / Pen-test language & evidence cadence

Samantha — thank you for the detail and spreadsheet. I reviewed Marissa's proposed positions and prepared contract-oriented edits. Key legal points: 

- Mutual audit rights should be scoped to information security and availability controls only and limited to (i) inspection of Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report, (ii) review of vendor-supplied pen-test attestation and remediation confirmation. We cannot agree to open-ended, on-site system audits.
- Pen-test coordination: Redwood asks for reasonable notice; Marissa suggested 15 business days. Mosaic proposed 30 days; we can accept 30 business days if the test will involve intrusive techniques or an expanded scope, otherwise 15 is standard.
- Evidence & indemnity: Redwood will provide evidence and remediation attestations but requests that any remediation costs arising from third-party tests that are beyond the agreed scope be handled separately (not auto-deducted from Redwood obligations).
- Confidentiality & redaction: any SOC 2 materials will be redacted to remove customer-specific PII and internal-only details.

I attached a tracked MSA+Exhibit redline with suggested language and a short comment summary. Suggested next steps: (1) Karthik to review for commercial acceptability, (2) Samantha to revert with Mosaic’s counter on notice window and remediation cost language, (3) if needed, short call between the counsels to finalize.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Karthik/Neha/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. A couple of clarifications from Mosaic: 

- We can accept tests against a non-production environment but Mosaic requires 30 calendar days notice for our procurement scheduling. If Redwood can confirm vendor attestation timelines (30 days remediation confirmation for critical items), we’re in.
- SOC 2 reports must be available via a secure portal (we cannot accept email attachments for final reports) — can Redwood support a portal link or SSO access for our security team?
- Regarding remediation costs: Mosaic will not ask Redwood to pay for remediation arising from tests that exceed the agreed scope. We just want assurance that critical findings will be remediated promptly and attested to.

We reviewed Neha’s edits offline and they look reasonable. Please provide the tracked redline to our counsel (LegalOps) and let us know an estimated calendar for final signature if these points hold. We are hopeful for a mid-July signature if both legal teams can align. Attaching Mosaic’s redline for your reference.
